messages:
kyle: Heads up — eu-west3 batch pool seeing a sustained local NVMe IOPS spike, ~3x baseline. GPU attaches are stalling (about 30% fail to bind). Noticed scrub/fstrim overlap recently.
maria: Which pool/cohort? any node IDs or logs?
kyle: scratchpool-cohort-9. Example from node gn-eu3-142: `nvme0 qdepth 256 -> 1024 qfull`, kernel logs show repeated fsync/backpressure. snippet: ```May 12 09:12:04 gn-eu3-142 kernel: blk_mq: I/O error, qdepth overflow
May 12 09:12:05 gn-eu3-142 janitor[2345]: scrub: read-errors=0, iops=62000, backlog=12```
raj: Ugh. Can we just throttle janitor/scrub cadence for that cohort? Avoid retiring if wear is low; cheaper to defer scrubs during peak.
kana: Agree. Propose: 1) pause scrub window for cohort-9 for 30m, 2) reroute new GPU attaches to eu-west3-dedicated-1 for 20m, 3) schedule proactive replacement only if SMART crosses threshold. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_iops_spike detected on scratchpool-cohort-9 (nodes: gn-eu3-138..gn-eu3-144). Autoscaler paused 4 attaches in last 10m.
ops-sre: +1 to throttle. Quick command to set janitor ratecap: ```curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/v1/janitor/ratecap -d '{"cohort":"cohort-9","iops_cap":30000,"duration":"30m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'```
kyle: Applying ratecap now. Will also tag hot nodes to avoid new preemptible attaches: `tag node gn-eu3-142 nvme:hot=true`.
maria: After ratecap applied, attach success rate jumped from 68% -> 92% in the last 5m. Nice.
raj: Cost note: shifting attaches to dedicated pool will add ~0.8c/token equivalent over baseline during this window — call it ~+$1.2k/day if prolonged. We should monitor and switch back asap.
kana: I'll run a short eval to confirm no regressions from deferring scrubs. If SMART trends up, we flip to retirement.
ops-sre: Logging decision and postmortem stub in #postmortems in case wear leads to later impact. For now we avoid node replacements. :clipboard:
kyle: TL;DR: throttle janitor for 30m, reroute new attaches to dedicated pool, monitor SMART & attach SLOs. I'll update if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
